messages:
Raj: heads-up, p99s spiked on prod around 20:02 UTC for the chat endpoint after the kernel-selector change. p50 ~ 90ms, p95 ~ 180ms, p99 ~ 980ms.
Amanda: ack. do we know which kernel path and request shape?
Raj: looks like long-context requests (~3.5k tokens) hitting the new fused-attn path. KV cache misses also higher for these sessions. stack samples show a lot of stalls in the GPU memcpy + small-microbatch overhead.
Leo: did the KV TTL change land this week? that could explain cache churn.
Sofia: yes, PR #4123 reduced KV TTL from 10m -> 2m to free memory for dedicated pools. rolled at 18:30.
Maya: oof. that TTL drop + fused kernel has worse startup cost for warmup + more kv rehydration. tail amplification looks plausible.
Carl: we profiled with perf-runner — attaching snippet:
```
--- perf dump ---
endpoint: /v1/chat/generate
model: redwood-13b-quant
microbatch_size: 8
median_seq_len: 512
p95_seq_len: 2100
kernel_path: fused_attn_v2
KV_cache_missed_pct: 12.4 -> 27.1 (after TTL change)
GPU memcpy stall: 42% of tail time
small batch overhead: +65ms per request under 1-4 microbatches
p99: 980ms -> baseline 320ms
```

Raj: suggested quick mitigations?
Amanda: short-term: cap max_tokens for hosted plan to 512 and enforce microbatch cap = 4 for the affected route. add a 700ms soft timeout with graceful truncation.
Leo: for truncation we should prefer truncating prefix and using KV-prefetch heuristics rather than dropping last tokens. dropping trailing tokens changes model output semantics more.
Sofia: agree. we can implement a policy: if remaining_tokens > 1024 and server latency approaching SLO, truncate the earliest context chunks (oldest) first and keep last N tokens + system prompt.
Maya: also add a fast-path kernel fallback: if seq_len > 2048 or KV_rehydration_rate > 15% then route to the legacy kernel with lower startup cost (slower per-token but better tail).
Carl: config proposal (canary):
```
{
  "route": "/v1/chat/generate",
  "canary": 0.05,
  "policies": {
    "microbatch_max": 4,
    "max_tokens_cap": 512,
    "soft_timeout_ms": 700,
    "truncation": "drop_earliest_chunks",
    "kernel_fallback": "legacy_attn_low_startup",
    "kv_ttl_threshold": "if_kv_miss_rate>0.15"
  }
}
```

Raj: sounds reasonable. rollout plan?
Amanda: canary 5% for 2h with extended tracing (sampler 1/10). monitor p95/p99 and error rates. if p99 improves and no QoR regressions flagged by Evals, ramp to 25% then 100% over 24h.
Sofia: will add an eval suite that compares last-token distributions for a sampled prompt set to catch quality regressions from truncation/fallback. send alerts on distribution drift > 2% KL.
Maya: on the infra side, we should revert the KV TTL change for dedicated pools if this persists; that buys time for smarter eviction and prefetch.
Carl: oncall-bot, can we schedule a hotfix rollout window and block other infra changes for the next 6h?
oncall-bot: Hotfix window scheduled by @Raj for 1772501500 -> 1772503900 UTC. Patch approval required from eng-runtime leads.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy queued for route /v1/chat/generate with config 1772501234-configA.
Raj: assigning actions: Amanda -> implement microbatch cap + soft timeout + truncation; Leo/Maya -> kernel fallback routing + perf test; Sofia -> eval checks and alerting; Carl -> KV TTL revert plan if needed and coordinate hotfix window.
Amanda: will open PRs for the runtime guardrails and add quick e2e test. ETA 2h. :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Leo: I'll add perf-runner scenarios for worst-case ctx and measure tail under both kernels.
Sofia: adding eval job now. will post results in this thread.
Maya: I'll watch prod during the canary and standby for rollback.
Raj: thanks — let's keep messages tight in this thread. quick update when canary is live or if p99 > 1s. :thumbsup:
